note: One question probes one dimension. Options map in facet order; display order is randomized per respondent.

questions.prompt: You have a free Saturday with nothing planned. What do you reach for first?

options.text: A project with my hands: fixing, building, cooking, training
A book, a problem or an idea I want to understand
A call or a get-together with people I care about

questions.prompt: A friend says, "Can you help me with something big?" What do you usually offer?

options.text: My time and effort on the ground
My thinking: a plan, an explanation, a second opinion
An introduction, my network or just being there with them

questions.prompt: When you picture your best asset, you think of:

options.text: My health, my tools, my home, my money in hand
What I know and how I think
The people who would show up for me

questions.prompt: You are new in a town. Your first move is to:

options.text: Learn the place by walking it and setting up my space
Read about it and learn how it works
Find the people: neighbors, groups, a first friend

questions.prompt: What do you tend to be praised for?

options.text: Getting real things done
Seeing what others miss
Making people feel welcome and trusted

questions.prompt: If you lost your job tomorrow, what would carry you through?

options.text: My savings, my skills with tools, my physical stamina
My expertise and my ability to learn fast
My contacts and my reputation

questions.prompt: Which kind of tiredness feels best?

options.text: After a hard physical day
After a long stretch of deep thinking
After a day full of good conversation

questions.prompt: You are given a budget to invest in yourself. You choose:

options.text: Equipment, a gym, a better workspace
A course, books, time to study
A community, a mentor, an event where I belong

questions.prompt: Others come to you when they need:

options.text: Something fixed, built or carried
An answer or an explanation
Someone to listen, connect or vouch

questions.prompt: A decision has to be made and you cannot have everything. What decides it?

options.text: What is right, even if it costs me
What is beautiful, fitting, true to its form
What works best for the result

questions.prompt: What bothers you most to see?

options.text: Someone treated unfairly
Something ugly or careless where care was possible
Time and effort wasted for nothing

questions.prompt: You are choosing a home. What matters most?

options.text: That it is a good place to raise good people
That it feels peaceful and looks right
That it is practical, affordable and well located

questions.prompt: A colleague takes a shortcut that works but bends a rule. You think:

options.text: It is wrong; the rule is there for a reason
The work is a bit sloppy; it should be done well
If it works and nobody is hurt, fine, but note the risk

questions.prompt: What would you want to be remembered for?

options.text: Doing right by others
Making something beautiful or meaningful
Getting important things done

questions.prompt: A story moves you most when it is about:

options.text: Sacrifice and doing what is right
Beauty, love, or something that has been lost
Someone who overcomes a hard problem

questions.prompt: When you give advice, you usually lead with:

options.text: What the right thing to do is
What feels true and fits who they are
What will actually work

questions.prompt: You have one hour to improve a shared space. You:

options.text: Fix what is unfair or unsafe for someone
Make it feel better: light, order, a nicer look
Remove what slows people down

questions.prompt: Your own best days feel:

options.text: Like I stood for something
Like I created or noticed something lovely
Like I got a lot of useful things done

questions.prompt: A plan falls apart halfway. Your first instinct is to:

options.text: Invent a new approach
Adjust quickly to what is in front of me
Go back to what is proven and steady it

questions.prompt: You are happiest when:

options.text: Starting something new
Things are changing and I can respond
Everything runs the way it should

questions.prompt: In a group project you naturally:

options.text: Propose the idea and start
Fill whatever gap appears
Keep it organized and on track

questions.prompt: Routine feels:

options.text: Like a cage unless I get to change it
Fine, as long as I can flex
Like solid ground

questions.prompt: When something works well, you:

options.text: Wonder how to make it different or bigger
Keep it, but adapt it to the next situation
Protect it and keep it going

questions.prompt: A friend asks how you handle surprises:

options.text: I turn them into new possibilities
I read the room and adjust
I would rather prevent them with a good system

questions.prompt: You are most likely to say:

options.text: "What if we tried something else?"
"Let's see what happens and adjust."
"Let's not break what works."

questions.prompt: When you set a goal, you tend to:

options.text: Reimagine it often as you learn
Keep it loose and respond to events
Break it into steady steps and keep going

questions.prompt: Your weak spot is more likely to be:

options.text: Starting more than I finish
Not committing to a direction
Resisting change when I should change
